# pr-1017: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1124
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T07:45:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 298

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

# pr-1017: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017

- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1124
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T07:45:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# pr-1017: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

content.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1124
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T07:45:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 298

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` line 51

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js` line 3079

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: E3 gap — a re-cancelled re-dispatch re-wedges the arm silently**

The once-per-head marker makes the ghost re-dispatch strictly one-shot per head: if the fresh CI run the machine dispatches here gets cancelled again (the gh-748 kicker race is not guaranteed to be gone — the incident that spawned this card was a cancel storm), the next tick finds `ghostProbe.isGhostCancel && ghostGateHeld` true, sees the marker, and takes t…

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1124
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T07:45:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js` line 298

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

---

### Thread 3 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

---

### Thread 5 — `js/unit-tests/test_smGithubSource.js` line 51

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.

---

### Thread 6 — `js/smAgent.js` line 3079

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: E3 gap — a re-cancelled re-dispatch re-wedges the arm silently**

The once-per-head marker makes the ghost re-dispatch strictly one-shot per head: if the fresh CI run the machine dispatches here gets cancelled again (the gh-748 kicker race is not guaranteed to be gone — the incident that spawned this card was a cancel storm), the next tick finds `ghostProbe.isGhostCancel && ghostGateHeld` true, sees the marker, and takes t…

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1017
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1017
- **Title**: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue
- **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot]
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1000` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +1124
- **Deletions**: -19
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T21:33:37Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-18T07:45:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1017._

> ℹ️ **3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

# pr-1017: gh-1000 Phantom ai_validating mutex holder blocks the whole agents validation queue

## Description

Closes #1000
### Root Cause
The `ai_validating` mutex holder set was derived from the provider's per-tick ioCache and never reconciled against the live label layer, so a vanished holder stayed a phantom turnstile deferring every validation candidate with `slots 1/1 taken`. Separately, a validation run concluding CANCELLED pre-materialization produced no check contexts, so `rerun_cancelled_checks` answered "nothing to rerun" — the arm wedged, the required check never re-reported, and the merge gate refused permanently (guest PR, no machine push to escape, gh-757).

### Fix
- `js/common/mutexRegistry.js` (new, pure): `derive` (I1 label-layer reconciliation), `reconcile` (I2 self-heal + alarm + counters), `recordPhantomHeal`/`mergeSnapshot` (factory-state carry), `conclusionMapping` (cancelled/timed_out → no verdict, re-dispatch), `isGhostCancelProbe` (AC3, gh-755 fresh-cancel grace).
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`: a full-slot defer decision re-derives holders against a live `github_list_prs` re-read; divergence ⇒ module-level ioCache self-heal (`smProvider.ioCacheDrop`), alarm line, holders corrected in the same query so a queued candidate arms in the same tick (AC2); probe failure keeps the cached decision one more tick (E4). Tick events drain via `takeMutexTickSnapshot()`.
- `js/smAgent.js`: `rerun_cancelled_checks` fetches the head workflow-runs rollup first; with no cancelled contexts it probes for a ghost cancel (newest dispatched run completed cancelled/timed_out, nothing active, grace elapsed) **and** the merge gate held by a missing/non-terminal required context — then re-dispatches fresh CI on the same head (`gh workflow run --ref`) with a once-per-head marker; publish rule merges the mutex metrics block across ticks.
- `js/factoryState.js`: additive `state.mutex` (counters + capped alarm tail, malformed blobs dropped); `js/common/validationLiveness.js`: silent-update failure marker helpers (I5 wiring point).
- Tests: `makeRequire` maps extended for the new module (test_smAgent / test_smGithubSource / test_mergeCadence).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_mutexRegistry.js` — 20 tests (AC1–AC3, I1–I3, alarm cap, snapshot carry) — PASS; was RED before the module existed.
- Full suite `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions.

### Notes
- Run-state conjunct of `derive(M)` stays with the gh-821 liveness sweep (single-writer rule); call sites pass the `noCompletedRuns` placeholder.
- Ghost re-dispatch is authorship-blind (plain workflow run on the head ref, no write to the guest branch); a failed `--ref` surfaces next tick with no marker posted.
- Ghost gate: all-terminal required contexts (green/red) suppress the probe — red belongs to fail_validation, a cancelled *context* to the existing rerun path (gh-682 kicker fixtures preserved).

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)

The CRAP gate requires running the unit suite instrumented with nyc, then running crap4js against coverage with the baseline. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2.
